messages:
support_agent_lucy: Heads-up — escalated ticket from Acme Maps: monthly invoice total is €0.03 lower than their dashboard sum. They attached request-level CSV. suspect per-request rounding + currency conversion order. posting their sample below

acme_maps_cs: Dashboard shows 12,345.670 tokens billed as €123.45 (rates page = 0.01 EUR per 1,000 tokens for this tier). Invoice line items sum to €123.42. small, but customer says it breaks reconciliation scripts and they need a clear cause. CSV snippet:```request_id,raw_tokens,usd_cost,eur_cost_line
r1,1234,0.01234,0.01
r2,11111,0.11111,0.11
TOTAL,12345,0.12345,0.12
```They also split VAT on separate lines per-region which they say changes the rounding outcome.

mia: Can you attach invoice id and invoice PDF? also which currency conversion timestamp did they use?

acme_maps_cs: invoice 2024-11-30-INV-8899, conversion timestamp 2024-11-30T23:59:59Z, VAT rate 20% on a separate VAT line. PDF attached to the ticket.

billing-bot: Automated note: invoices are generated by summing per-request EUR amounts (converted from USD micro-units) and rounding each line to 2 decimals before aggregation. See docs: /billing/rounding-policy v2.

alex: This reads like the classic "per-request round then sum" vs "sum then round" problem. If you round each converted line to cents before summing, you can lose a few cents across thousands of rows. VAT split into its own line (rounded separately) can amplify the residual.

sam: Quick repro I ran locally with their CSV — two aggregation modes show the difference. Snippet:```python
from decimal import Decimal, ROUND_HALF_UP
lines = [Decimal('0.01234'), Decimal('0.11111')]
# per-line rounding
per_line = sum([l.quantize(Decimal('0.01'), rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP) for l in lines])
# invoice-level rounding
invoice_sum = sum(lines).quantize(Decimal('0.01'), rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP)
print('per_line', per_line)  # 0.12
print('invoice_level', invoice_sum)  # 0.12
# add more lines (simulate thousands) -> difference emerges
```

alex: Note the example above is tiny; with many micro-values you'll hit a drift. Also currency conversion ordering matters: converting per-request with a float conversion then rounding to cents is lossy compared to summing raw micro-units (e.g., micro-euros) then dividing and rounding once.

support_agent_lucy: Customer is asking for explanation and either a corrected invoice or a one-time credit. Can we confirm the code path that generated invoice 2024-11-30-INV-8899?

alex: I'll pull the generation run logs. Probable sequence: (1) convert raw USD microcosts to EUR by applying FX rate and rounding per-request to 2 decimals, (2) emit line items and VAT separately, (3) sum printed lines for total. If so, that matches the delta.

mia: If that's true we should treat as a billing defect and offer a small credit; also adjust pipeline to accumulate in the smallest currency unit and only round at invoice-level (or keep a controlled per-request policy with documented reconciliation guidance).

jordan: I'm OK with a one-time credit for the rounding delta. Support — please offer provisional credit of €0.05 to the customer and mark ticket as billing-escalated. Engineering to prioritize a fix in the next billing run to compute totals with integer math.

support_agent_lucy: Will do. @acme_maps_cs — we can apply a €0.05 credit now and follow up with an updated invoice if engineering confirms a regeneration path. Sorry for the trouble :handshake:��

acme_maps_cs: Thanks, appreciate the speedy response. Can you also confirm how future invoices will behave? we reconcile programmatically.

alex: Short answer: we're moving to invoice-level rounding from micro-units for aggregated charges and will publish the change in the billing changelog and /billing/rounding-policy. I will post a PR with a repro test that asserts no residuals > 0.05 EUR per monthly invoice for common workloads.

sam: Added a quick unit test that compares both methods across randomized microvalues and fails if difference > 0.05 EUR. Pushed to internal branch billing/rounding-fix.

jordan: Thanks team. Support, confirm the credit and close after customer ack. Eng please follow up with timeline for release and a short note for the changelog.

support_agent_lucy: Credit applied (refund tx id REF-20241101-332). Customer acknowledged and will re-open if anything else shows up. Closing ticket but keeping billing-escalation open for the fix.

alex: Follow-up action items: 1) convert billing pipeline to integer accumulation (microcents) and single rounding step, 2) expand tests to include VAT-split scenarios and multi-currency conversions, 3) publish guidance on how we show per-request vs invoice numbers in dashboard vs PDF.

sam: Filed ENG-6543 and linked to the ticket. ETA for patch to staging: 2 weeks.

jordan: noted. good work everyone :tada:
